atAGlance: Vietnamese beef stew with warm spices, carrot, lemongrass, and tender beef, eaten with bread, noodles, or rice depending on the shop.
whatItIs: Bò kho is not just “beef stew” in a Western sense; it is perfumed with lemongrass, star anise, cinnamon, annatto oil, and fish sauce, with beef cooked until spoon-tender.
howToEnjoy: Tear off pieces of bánh mì and dip them into the broth, or order the noodle version if you want a fuller bowl. Add basil, lime, and chili slowly so you do not cover the spice of the stew.
howLocalsOrder: Order bò kho with bánh mì, noodles, or rice depending on how you want to eat the broth. Ask for extra bread, less chili, or more carrots before serving.
worthKnowing: Bò kho is a beloved breakfast and lunch dish, especially in southern Vietnam, and it shows how Vietnamese cooks make French-era bread feel entirely local.
goodToKnow: Ask whether the shop serves it with bánh mì, hủ tiếu, or mì if you have a preference.
